prompt: What does Angular do during change detection?

choices.text: It reloads the component's data from the server
choices.why: Loading is the resource's or the service's job; the walk only reads the classes.

choices.text: Re-reads every template, then fixes the DOM
choices.why: Right. It walks the tree and compares.

choices.text: It recompiles the templates that changed on disk
choices.why: That is the dev server rebuilding, not change detection.

choices.text: It destroys and recreates every component
choices.why: Components survive a walk; only the DOM values that differ are touched.

prompt: `label()` was called again after a click on a button whose handler does nothing. Why?

choices.text: The click changed `label`'s return value for this one time
choices.why: It returns the same text every time.

choices.text: `look` reloaded the page after it clicked the button
choices.why: The page loaded once; the extra calls came from walks.

choices.text: Events schedule walks, and methods are asked again
choices.why: Right. Angular cannot know a method's answer without calling it.

choices.text: Methods in templates are run on a timer by Angular
choices.why: There is no timer; walks happen when something schedules them.

prompt: In development mode, why does Angular walk the tree twice in a row?

choices.text: To check nothing changed between the walks
choices.why: Right. A difference is the `NG0100` error.

choices.text: Because the first walk only reads and the second one writes the DOM
choices.why: Each walk does both; the second only compares.

choices.text: To warm up the cache before production
choices.why: Development builds are not a warm-up for production ones.

choices.text: Because zone.js is loaded twice
choices.why: The planner has no zone.js, and the second walk happened anyway.

prompt: Under zone.js, the default component's plain field showed 1 after its timer. What told Angular to walk?

choices.text: The field, which notifies Angular when assigned
choices.why: A plain field notifies nobody; that is a signal's job.

choices.text: zone.js's own `setTimeout`
choices.why: Right. It had replaced the browser's timer with one that tells Angular.

choices.text: The browser, which redraws the page every second
choices.why: The browser draws the DOM; it knows nothing of the class's fields.

choices.text: `look`, which clicks the page while it waits
choices.why: `--wait` only waits.

prompt: Which cost of zone.js does the lesson name?

choices.text: It cannot run in Chromium, only in older browsers
choices.why: It ran in Chromium in this very lesson.

choices.text: It makes every field in every component a signal
choices.why: It changes nothing about fields; it wraps the browser's asynchronous functions.

choices.text: It forbids OnPush in any component
choices.why: OnPush was designed for zone.js applications.

choices.text: Extra code, and walks after everything
choices.why: Right. Whether anything changed or not.

prompt: `npm audit` blamed `undici` and offered `npm audit fix --force`. Why does the lesson advise against running it?

choices.text: It would delete the lockfile
choices.why: The objection is what it installs, not the lockfile.

choices.text: It would install `@angular/build` 20, a major backwards
choices.why: Right. For a library that only runs while you build.

choices.text: `undici` is part of zone.js, and removing it breaks the bench
choices.why: `undici` belongs to the CLI's build system, not to zone.js.

choices.text: Audit reports are always false alarms
choices.why: The advisories are real; the proposed fix is out of proportion.

prompt: Under zone.js, the OnPush component's plain field stayed 0 after its timer. Why?

choices.text: zone.js does not patch timers inside OnPush components
choices.why: The same timer triggered a walk; the walk skipped the component.

choices.text: Nothing marked it, so the walk skipped it
choices.why: Right. A timer setting a plain field is not one of the things that mark.

choices.text: OnPush components are only checked once, at creation
choices.why: They are checked whenever marked; this one never was.

choices.text: The timer threw an error inside the OnPush component
choices.why: There was no error; the value simply was not read again.

prompt: Which of these mark an OnPush component so the next walk visits it? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: A signal its template reads changes
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: A `(click)` bound in its template fires
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: A plain field changes in a timer
choices.why: That is exactly what stayed 0.

choices.text: `markForCheck()` is called
choices.why: Right. The escape hatch older code is full of.

choices.text: An array it received is changed in place
choices.why: Same identity, so no change by OnPush's rule.

prompt: A parent passes `sessions` to an OnPush child, then pushes a session into the same array. Why does the child not update?

choices.text: OnPush children ignore inputs
choices.why: They react to an input that changes to a new value.

choices.text: Same array, so by identity no change
choices.why: Right. The same rule as a signal's `Object.is`, from lesson 6.

choices.text: `push` is not allowed on arrays passed as inputs
choices.why: It is allowed, and that is the trap.

choices.text: The parent must call `markForCheck()` on itself
choices.why: Marking the parent does not change the child's input.

prompt: Without zone.js, which line of the bench still showed 1?

choices.text: `default, plain field`
choices.why: Nothing told Angular the plain field changed.

choices.text: `OnPush, plain field`
choices.why: It stayed 0 under zone.js already.

choices.text: `OnPush, signal`
choices.why: Right. Setting the signal marked its component and scheduled a walk.

choices.text: None of them, until the page was reloaded
choices.why: The signal line updated without a reload.

prompt: Moving an old application to zoneless, which failure does the lesson warn is silent?

choices.text: The build failing on every plain field
choices.why: The build has no opinion on plain fields.

choices.text: An error in the console on every timer
choices.why: Nothing is logged; that is the problem.

choices.text: Fields set asynchronously going stale
choices.why: Right. They show their old value until something else triggers a walk.

choices.text: Tests passing that used to fail
choices.why: The lesson's concern is the screen, not the test results.

prompt: Match each event with whether it schedules a walk in a zoneless application.

pairs.left: a signal read by a template is set
pairs.right: marks the component and schedules a walk
its value signal changes and schedules a walk

right_distractors: the mouse moves over the page

prompt: Since Angular 21, a new project created with `ng new` uses no ___ at all.
`{{ now() }}`, where `now()` returns `Date.now()`, produced `NG0100`. Why is that a bug and not a false alarm?

choices.text: The clock cannot be read from inside an Angular template
choices.why: It can; reading it on every walk is the problem.

choices.text: `Date.now()` is too slow to be called from a template
choices.why: Speed is not the issue; changing answers are.

choices.text: The screen shows one answer while the state holds another
choices.why: Right. Screen and state disagree, and production would not say so.

choices.text: Development mode adds random delays between the two walks
choices.why: There is no added delay; the two walks are milliseconds apart.

prompt: The error Angular's development mode reports when a template expression gives a different answer on the second walk is NG___.

choices.text: Only in the console, in development mode
choices.why: Right. The page drew the first value and carried on.

choices.text: On the page, in place of the paragraph
choices.why: The paragraph showed a number.

choices.text: In `ng build`'s output, as a template error
choices.why: The build cannot know what a method returns at run time.

choices.text: In production as well, as a warning
choices.why: Production skips the second walk entirely.

choices.text: Every existing component became OnPush
choices.why: Existing files were edited by hand in this lesson; the command touches `angular.json` only.

choices.text: The default for components `ng generate` writes
choices.why: Right. New components start with OnPush.

choices.text: Angular's change detection for the whole application
choices.why: Change detection is configured per component, and the app was already zoneless.

choices.text: The TypeScript compiler's strictness
choices.why: That is `tsconfig.json`, unrelated.

prompt: Put the steps of moving an old zone.js application to zoneless in the order the lesson gives.
items: make components OnPush one at a time, fixing what goes stale
run every test and look at every screen

prompt: A library calls your callback when a file finishes uploading, and your component sets `this.progress = 100` there. In the zoneless planner, what do you write instead?

choices.text: The same line, followed by `setTimeout(() => {})` to trigger a walk
choices.why: An empty timer schedules nothing without zone.js.

choices.text: `import 'zone.js'` at the top of the component
choices.why: That would bring back the whole cost to fix one field.

choices.text: `this.progress.set(100)`, with `progress` a signal
choices.why: Right. The signal marks the component and schedules the walk.

choices.text: Nothing: callbacks from libraries always trigger a walk
choices.why: Only what Angular trusts triggers a walk; a library's callback is not on the list.
